Core thesis

The conductor becomes the diagnostic substrate.

SINE~WaiV is not positioned as another attached sensor. It is a software-defined electrical diagnostic layer that exploits electromechanical coupling between mechanical state, air-gap field behavior, load modulation, and stator-current spectra.

Market-facing phrase
Wire-as-Sensor / Passive diagnostic infrastructure.
Technical phrase
Current-domain virtual sensing through electromechanical coupling.
Phase I scope

Revolutionary thesis. Narrow proof target.

The Phase I question is deliberately precise: can SINE~WaiV separate asset-specific mechanical degradation signatures from grid-side and VFD-side artifacts using only motor-current observations?

NSF / investor fit

From diagnostic tool to infrastructure layer.

SINE~WaiV's advantage is not merely fault classification. The strategic claim is broader: existing industrial power infrastructure may become a scalable machine-health observability layer, allowing customers to extend predictive-maintenance coverage without instrumenting every asset individually.

Intellectual merit

Tests the electromechanical observability problem in current-domain signals under realistic contamination.

Broader impacts

Expands access to predictive maintenance for SMEs and facilities operating legacy equipment.

Commercial potential

Lowers deployment friction, service burden, and total monitoring cost compared with per-asset sensor networks.
